scope: Controller-mediated diagnostic LPDDR4 MRR of immutable identity/geometry registers; not PHY training
board_test_scope: Identity MRR under Linux with DRAM initialized by the existing legacy boot chain; not cold initialization

public_sources.facts: lpddr4_mr_read: MRCTRL0 rank mask at bits5:4, read bit0, trigger bit31; MRCTRL1 MA at bits15:8; MRSTAT bit0 must be idle before commands. NXP receive monitor registers are NOT used on T736.

lpddr4_mr_read and dram_info_init read trained LP4 MRs without PHY mux changes, MR13 changes, or AXI disable. Polls MRSTAT after trigger, then an NXP-specific receive-valid bit. MSTR active ranks are bits25:24. This supports controller scheduling with initialized DRAM; it is not a T736 hardware test.
Software MR transactions precede AXI port disable. STAT operating_mode1 is normal. MR13 bit7 FSP-OP, bit6 FSP-WR, bit3 VRCG are FSP/Vref control, not MRR enable.

read_only_sdk_register_reference.transaction: wait MRSTAT[0]=0; MRCTRL0=(1<<(rank+4))|1; MRCTRL1=MA<<8; MRCTRL0=(1<<(rank+4))|0x80000001; wait MRCTRL0[31]=0
read_only_sdk_register_reference.valid_or_error_bit: None read by this helper; no independent T736 definition found
read_only_sdk_register_reference.caller_context: save_phy_2d_training_result also reads PHY CSRs under mux0 and sets type8 MR13=0xc8 before MR14 readout, restoring MR13=0x80 and mux1 afterward. These are training/FSP/Vref operations, not part of the MRR helper; they are intentionally excluded from identity reads.

implementation_guards: MR5, MR6, MR8 only; no generic MRW or arbitrary-MMIO entry point
channel0/1, rank0/1; MSTR low type nibble2 and selected active-rank bit required
STAT normal required before command and after completion; nonnormal state rejected without mode changes
MRSTAT busy or MRCTRL0 trigger already set: return busy before writing
Exactly three writes restricted to channel MRCTRL0/MRCTRL1; MRCTRL0 read bit always1; only one rank selected
Both trigger-clear and busy-clear required; selected rank and read bit checked during completion
One global bounded wait1..10000us with callback failure handling; result unchanged on every failure
No timeout reset/retry/cleanup that could race a still-pending transaction
Returns raw32 plus board-type8 selected lane byte; does not infer manufacturer or memory density from an unvalidated response
caller_prerequisites: DRAM controller, DFI and PHY already initialized and trained
Caller owns and serializes software MR interface and prevents concurrent controller/DVFS reconfiguration
MMIO callbacks provide device memory ordering and report access failure
Repeat MR5/MR6/MR8 across ranks/channels and inspect raw values; idle completion alone cannot prove fresh receive latch
not_established: T736 receive-latch valid/error/clear bits and exact latching clock latency
Distinct physical rank/channel routing: all targets report identical manufacturer/revision/geometry
Alias-free capacity and DDR training quality
Full LP4 initialization, PHY CA executor, training firmware, and cold boot

hardware_identity_observation_20261114.decode: Micron; vendor revision ID1=7 (no exact part inference); MR8 S16/16n, x16 per channel, 16Gb per channel. Conditional on the already observed 2-channel/2-rank topology, 2*2*16Gb/8=8GiB.
hardware_identity_observation_20261114.freshness: Distinct ff/07/18 values follow both MR request orders. This supports command-dependent fresh readout and excludes a single unchanged latch or simple one-request lag across these requests; it does not identify a receive-valid bit or independently distinguish identical physical ranks.
hardware_identity_observation_20261114.datasheet: Micron z19m_embedded_lpddr4_lpddr4x.pdf Rev.G 04/2022, Tables35/37/41, pages55/56; source URL and independent U-Boot corroboration are in the analysis JSON.
